question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables 

$$
u=y-2x,\,v=y+x,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the lines

$$
y=2x-1,\,y=2x+1,\,y=1-x,\,y=2-x.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=y-2x,\,v=y+x
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

We substitute $u=y-2x$ into the equations of the first and second lines:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y=2x-1 & ⟹\, & y-2x=-1 & ⟹\, & u=-1 \\  & y=2x+1 & ⟹\, & y-2x=1 & ⟹\, & u=1\end{aligned}
$$

And we substitute $v=y+x$ into the equations of the third and fourth lines:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y=1-x & ⟹\, & y+x=1 & ⟹\, & v=1 \\  & y=2-x & ⟹\, & y+x=2 & ⟹\, & v=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,1\le v\le 2\}
$$

![](images/21/2116f558e3712a08c13d49238054336dcb60efc7d9602bed220be8115d392be7.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & \text{ }\text{ }1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|-\frac{1}{3}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{∬}_{Δ}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \text{Area}(Δ) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{1}{xy},\,v={x}^{2}y,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the curves

$$
y=\frac{1}{2x},\,y=\frac{1}{3x},\,y=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},\,y=\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=\frac{1}{xy},\,v={x}^{2}y
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

We substitute $u=\frac{1}{xy}$ into the equations of the first and second curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{1}{2x} & ⟹\, & \frac{1}{xy}=2 & ⟹\, & u=2 \\  & y=\frac{1}{3x} & ⟹\, & \frac{1}{xy}=3 & ⟹\, & u=3\end{aligned}
$$

And we substitute $v={x}^{2}y$ into the equations of the third and fourth curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} & ⟹\, & {x}^{2}y=1 & ⟹\, & v=1 \\  & y=\frac{3}{{x}^{2}} & ⟹\, & {x}^{2}y=3 & ⟹\, & v=3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,2\le u\le 3,\,1\le v\le 3\}
$$

![](images/05/05d2ca47db245b147cb52f95a474a60ece144931c8b6e1e40c6628a99b53d690.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}y} & -\frac{1}{x{y}^{2}} \\ 2xy & \text{ }\text{ }{x}^{2}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=y=\frac{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}y}=\frac{1}{{u}^{2}v}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}v}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}v}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{v}\,\text{d}v \\  & =(-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2})\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡3.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}},\,v=\frac{{y}^{2}}{x},
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the curves

$$
y={x}^{2},\,y=3{x}^{2},\,x={y}^{2},\,x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}},\,v=\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

We substitute $u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}$ into the equations of the first and second curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y={x}^{2} & ⟹\, & \frac{y}{{x}^{2}}=1 & ⟹\, & u=1 \\  & y=3{x}^{2} & ⟹\, & \frac{y}{{x}^{2}}=3 & ⟹\, & u=3\end{aligned}
$$

And we substitute $v=\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}$ into the equations of the third and fourth curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & x={y}^{2} & ⟹\, & \frac{{y}^{2}}{x}=1 & ⟹\, & v=1 \\  & x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & ⟹\, & \frac{{y}^{2}}{x}=4 & ⟹\, & v=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 3,\,1\le v\le 4\}
$$

![](images/26/26eaba24af54a40f59f92148c145285ba4097ce765aee8cfc9a6241ff88b9498.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-\frac{2y}{{x}^{3}} & \frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ -\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} & \text{ }\text{ }\frac{2y}{x}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-\frac{3{y}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=-\frac{{x}^{4}}{3{y}^{2}}=-\frac{1}{3{u}^{2}}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|-\frac{1}{3{u}^{2}}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u{\int }_{1}^{4}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}+1)\cdot (4-1) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{{x}^{2}}{y},\,v=xy,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the curves

$$
y={x}^{2},\,y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{3},\,y=\frac{2}{x},\,y=\frac{4}{x}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=\frac{{x}^{2}}{y},\,v=xy
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

We substitute $u=\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}$ into the equations of the first and second curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y={x}^{2} & ⟹\, & \frac{{x}^{2}}{y}=1 & ⟹\, & u=1 \\  & y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{3} & ⟹\, & \frac{{x}^{2}}{y}=3 & ⟹\, & u=3\end{aligned}
$$

And we substitute $v=xy$ into the equations of the third and fourth curves:

$$
\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{2}{x} & ⟹\, & xy=2 & ⟹\, & v=2 \\  & y=\frac{4}{x} & ⟹\, & xy=4 & ⟹\, & v=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 3,\,2\le v\le 4\}
$$

![](images/12/1207d8cdb8afd7c55d712caca043edfe9f0d0395343a6cbd329cf5861ec3bce7.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{2x}{y} & -\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} \\ y & \text{ }\text{ }x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=\frac{y}{3{x}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{1}{3u}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u{\int }_{2}^{4}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (4-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3.\end{aligned}
$$
